id: Scenic Soundscape Presents Broderbeats Live From The Remutaka Range-Massey Cinema, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Scenic Soundscape Presents Broderbeats Live From The Remutaka Range
long_description:
Scenic Soundscape presents broderbeats live from the Remutaka

Join us for the screening of Scenic Soundscape Episode 02 at the Massey University Cinema.

This place is where it all started for Lennox. A remote trig with breathtaking views of the Remutaka. We climbed Te Ara Tirohanga, the Remutaka Trig Walk, in the dark. Crew, DJ decks, cameras, drones and battery rigs, all carried up at 4AM to catch the first light.

The result is a one hour film where you can expect to hear from someone very close to him about the whenua and what it means to them. Then you’ll watch the performance, filmed live as the sun comes up. Raw and emotional on a ridge line with nothing but 360 views of the Wairarapa.

Stick around after for a Q&A with Jean Thoral (Scenic Soundscape founder) and Lennox (broderbeats), hosted by Cushla Aston. Lennox is currently on his INTUITION Volume 3 NZ tour, wrapping up with a date in Fiji. If you want to see/witness the origins of Volume 3, this is one to watch.

DETAILS

Doors 6:30PM
Film starts 7:30PM sharp
End: 9PM
Bar with snacks and drinks if you get here early
Plenty of parking on site
Warning dancing might occur

Made possible with the support of the French Embassy in New Zealand, CentrePort, Fujifilm, The Arts Foundation, Massey University and YOU.

Tickets via humanitix

id: Thriller Thursday-Moon Bar, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Thriller Thursday
long_description:
Come get a little spooky with three of Pōneke's finest alt rock groups. A great lineup of up-n-comers and established baddies, bringing the energy and attitude to the Moon stage on a Thursdee.


DEAD CHERRY are making waves with their high energy slice of old school rock ‘n roll, keeping it raw and real. Their debut EP Mother was released late last year. Fast, heavy, fun, and emotive, their live shows are not to be missed.


SEISMIC STATE are high-octane alt-rock with a blues-funk soul. A staple of the New Zealand rock circuit, the Wellington quartet is known for a professional, high-energy live show. Since the release of their debut EP State of Things, which earned international airplay and a Top 58 spot on The Generator FM’s Kiwi 101, the band has consistently anchored bills at iconic venues including San Fran and Valhalla.


STEERPYKE are a three-piece band playing a mix of originals and off-beat covers in and around the darker end of the post-punk genre. Formed in Wellington during COVID19, Nigel Baxter (bass, vox) and Adam Gray (guitar, vox) originally met on a Weekend Warriors session. James Gilberd, drummer and stalwart of the local alternative music scene, joined in 2023. They reached the regional finals of Battle of the Bands in 2026.

id: Mudhoney | Wellington-Meow Nui, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Mudhoney | Wellington
long_description:
For the first time in over a decade, Mudhoney return to New Zealand for a run of intimate shows. Renowned for their ferocious live performances, the band continue to deliver the same high-voltage mix of sludgy riffs, pounding rhythms and Mark Arm's unmistakable snarl that made them one of the most influential rock bands of their era.
﻿
Formed in Seattle in 1988, Mudhoney helped define the sound that would become known as grunge, combining garage rock, punk and heavy distortion into something raw, loud and entirely their own. As one of the cornerstone acts of legendary independent label Sub Pop, the band became a crucial influence on the explosion of alternative rock that followed, with tracks like 'Touch Me I'm Sick' and 'Suck You Dry' remaining enduring underground classics.

﻿More than 35 years on, Mudhoney remain as vital as ever, continuing to release acclaimed new music and proving night after night why they are regarded as one of the greatest live rock bands of their generation.

﻿When it comes to grunge, or even just Seattle, I think there was one band that made the definitive music of the time. It wasn't us or Nirvana, but Mudhoney. Nirvana delivered it to the world, but Mudhoney were the band of that time and sound. – Eddie Vedder (Pearl Jam)

﻿A rare chance to experience genuine grunge royalty up close.

id: Tape Night-Pyramid Club, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Tape Night
long_description:
TAPE NIGHT featuring:
Donna van Talgon
George D Angus
Indigogue Browne

Pyramid Club is happy to present a night of analogue tape misadventures and manipulations.

Donna van Talgon (aka. Izzy Fyfe/youbeepastablaster) is a musician and sound maker from Ōtepoti/Dunedin who uses multi-speed cassette tape transcription machines to warp found cassettes and home recordings. Matt Middleton of Crude fame describes their music as a Watersian descent into the mind of madness, chronozone. Utter postmodernism, samples from multifarious eras and ethnicities and qualities gratuitously reworked on-a-whim, a mixture of pure noise and cuts of electronic, a juggernaut, a plunderphonic ride into irregularity, dissonance, discord, deconstruction, re-absorption, loops.
https://youtu.be/msoZ7CPt22w

George D Angus (aka. Daniel Beban) is a BBC trained tape operator who has several decades of experience in coaxing absurdist sound collages out of reel-to-reel tape machines, including three releases of tape music on Thrill Jockey with Alexander Tucker as Imbogodom.

Indigogue Browne is a multidisciplinary artist and filmmaker producing chaotic semi-improvised sparkly harsh noise-pop and omnichord meanderings.


Special thanks to Creative NZ and Wellington City Council for supporting Pyramid Club's programme.

id: Induna - Favourite Colours (Release Show)-MOON, Wellington -Under The Radar
name: Induna - Favourite Colours (Release Show)
long_description:
Following recent performances supporting internationally acclaimed Nigerian artist Seun Kuti & Egypt 80, Aotearoa-based South African artist InDuna is set to release his new single 'Favourite Colours' and celebrates with a special headline show at Moon, Newtown, Wellington on Friday 30th October 2026.

Blending Afro-pop, R&B and folk, InDuna's live show brings infectious rhythms and uplifting energy alongside the more personal stories behind the songs. 'Favourite Colours' is an atmospheric anthem about identity, healing and resilience, using colour as a metaphor for how anxiety, grief and disconnection can drain the vibrancy from life, and the journey back to yourself.

InDuna will be joined by a special guest support act, to be announced.

Wheelchair accessible, seated and standing available.

About InDuna
Artist and producer InDuna draws on his South African roots, raised between Johannesburg and Limpopo before moving to Aotearoa at fourteen. His sound fuses African rhythm with contemporary pop and electronic production. Highlights include the King's Trust Young Global Achiever Award (2024), his single 'Dreams' (Best Original Song, International Online Web Fest; Official NZ Hot Singles Chart; featured in 'Ink and Gold'), and his 2025 EP 'Go High' (#16, Official Top 20 Aotearoa Albums Chart). He's supported Seun Kuti & Egypt 80 and opened for JessB, Estère and Deva Mahal, with headline shows across Wellington and Auckland.

'Favourite Colours' is supported by New Zealand On Air.
